# RFC 2578 section 7.1.4 defines BITS as a collection of named bits, and
# the name is bound to the number the definition writes, not to where the
# name appears in the list. So alpha, gamma and delta are bits 0, 4 and 7
# — never 0, 1 and 2 — and an agent reporting bit 4 is reporting gamma.
#
# RFC 2578 section 7.9 gives the DEFVAL form for BITS as a bit list inside
# the value's own braces, which makes "{ { } }" the way to say no bit is
# set. Both spellings appear below because a parser that reads the outer
# braces as an OID would take the empty one for a malformed OID.

dialect TEST-BITS-MIB SMIv2

oid            TEST-BITS-MIB.features 1.3.6.1.4.1.47001.1
syntax-base    TEST-BITS-MIB.features BITS
syntax-members TEST-BITS-MIB.features alpha(0) gamma(4) delta(7)

oid            TEST-BITS-MIB.namedFeatures 1.3.6.1.4.1.47001.2
syntax-name    TEST-BITS-MIB.namedFeatures FeatureBits
syntax-base    TEST-BITS-MIB.namedFeatures BITS
syntax-members TEST-BITS-MIB.namedFeatures alpha(0) gamma(4) delta(7)

type-base      TEST-BITS-MIB.FeatureBits BITS
type-members   TEST-BITS-MIB.FeatureBits alpha(0) gamma(4) delta(7)

# The contiguous list is here as the control: it is the shape under which
# reading positions off declaration order and reading declared numbers
# give the same answer, so it must not be the only shape a suite covers.
oid            TEST-BITS-MIB.contiguousFeatures 1.3.6.1.4.1.47001.3
syntax-members TEST-BITS-MIB.contiguousFeatures first(0) second(1) third(2)
